newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-STOLTENBERG SERVICE ERRORS SAVE CHANG IN SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-STOLTENBERG SERVICE ERRORS SAVE CHANG IN SEMIFINAL.

text.p: A pair of critical double faults sank Australian Jason Stoltenberg and helped save top seed Michael Chang, who advanced to Sunday's final against Grant Stafford at the U.S. Men's Clay Court Championships.
Chang took advantage of Stoltenberg's mistakes to win their semifinal 4-6 6-3 6-3.
Stafford, an unseeded South African, defeated sixth-seeded American Chris Woodruff 6-3 4-6 6-4 in the other semifinal.
Stafford will be looking for his first career title on Sunday. Chang has won three titles already in 1997 and can claim a 30th career tournament triumph if he wins on Sunday.
The fifth-seeded Stoltenberg, last year's Wimbledon semifinalist, missed chances in the second set to break Chang and serve for a 5-1 lead.

Lost opportunities plagued the Australian again in the third set. Stoltenberg double-faulted to drop serve in the fifth game, then double-faulted again to go match point down trailing 5-3. Chang won the match on the next point when Stoltenberg hit a backhand deep.

The start of play was delayed by over six hours as the second major storm of the week swept through the area. Both Chang and Stoltenberg struggled to find their rhythm early on after the delay but Stoltenberg won the first set 6-4 with a backhand winner.

Chang trailed 3-1 in the second set and double-faulted to give Stoltenberg a chance for 4-1. But the Australian missed the opportunity to break and instead it was Chang who broke Stoltenberg in the next game.
Chang broke again for 5-3 then served out the set 6-3 when Stoltenberg missed a backhand.
Chang started to go for winners more often in the third set, but in the end it was poor serving by Stoltenberg which gave Chang the chance to capitalise and win the match 6-3 in the third set.
"I think these matches are really good for me," said Chang, who will jump one spot to number two in the world on Sunday.
"When you play a lot of tough matches it's going to get you into the clay season a lot quicker. I feel I can definitely play better on clay," said Chang.
Stafford, ranked 73, had won only two matches ever on clay before entering this event.
"I used to get down on myself on clay and get mad about it," Stafford said after the one hour, 49 minute match in which the South African lost his first set of the tournament.
"Having a positive attitude has helped me win a lot of points on clay."
